_comment: Scene sequences for seven video genres. A genre is a starting skeleton, not a rule —
copy the `scenes` array of the one you want into your script.json and fill the inputs.
`local` is the GEOGRAPHY one. The kit also has skills/geo-optimize, which is the OTHER
thing called GEO — writing so an answer engine can quote you. Same acronym, different
job, and the two never appear in the same task.
Why this file exists: VIDEO_SCRIPT.template.json shows the SHAPE of a script, and the
catalogue shows what each template does, but neither answers the question someone
actually has — 'I want to make a review, which frames and in what order?'. Picking a
sequence from scratch every time is how every video ends up looking the same, because
the first three templates in the list are the ones that get used.
Each genre names its templates and the beat each one carries. Durations come from the
narration at render time; `voiceText` is what you write.

review.label: Review sản phẩm / dịch vụ
review.whenToUse: You tried something and have a verdict. The score frame is the payload; everything before it is setup.

beats.beat: The verdict, spoiled. Nobody watches a review to be kept in suspense.
What it is, in one line, over footage of the thing.
The belief this review overturns. Skip it if the verdict confirms what everyone already thinks — there is nothing to strike out.
The number that justifies the verdict — speed, price, battery, whatever you measured.
Score, verdict, pros and cons. The frame people screenshot.
Who it is for, who it is not for.

tutorial.label: Hướng dẫn từng bước
tutorial.whenToUse: Someone wants to do the thing. Show the steps, then show it working.

beats.beat: The outcome, not the topic. 'Agent tự đăng bài' beats 'Hôm nay nói về automation'.
Three to five steps. More than five, split into a second scene.
The hardest step as the actual command, plus the error people hit — frame-screenshot if the step happens in a browser instead.
Where to get it, and the one thing to try first. A tutorial that ends without a next step gets watched and forgotten.

news.label: Bản tin
news.whenToUse: Something happened. Say what, then why it matters.

beats.beat: The event in one sentence.
The one number that makes it news.
How it got here. The gap between the dates is half the story, which a list of steps cannot show.
What changes for the viewer specifically.
A question worth answering in the comments.

listicle.label: Danh sách N thứ
listicle.whenToUse: A ranked or grouped set. The count is the promise; keep it.

beats.beat: The count and the category. '5 công cụ' — and then deliver five.
The list itself, numbered, arriving one at a time.
The two that are hardest to choose between, side by side.
What to do with the list — and what not to. Advice with no score attached.
The one you would pick, and why.

launch.label: Ra mắt sản phẩm
launch.whenToUse: You built something and it is now available. The beat everything is arranged around is the moment it gets named — before that the viewer does not know what you are talking about, and after it they either care or they do not.

beats.beat: The problem, in one sentence, arriving a word at a time. Not the product — nobody has a reason to care about it yet.
How it was against how it is. The gap between the two is the whole argument for the thing existing.
The name, finally. This is the frame the video was built to arrive at.
What it actually does — two or three capabilities, not a feature list.
Where to get it. One link, one action.

testimonial.label: Câu chuyện khách hàng
testimonial.whenToUse: Someone else's result. Their words carry it; yours frame it.

beats.beat: The result, as a number or a before/after.
Their words, credited. Do not paraphrase — a cleaned-up quote sounds written.
How it was actually said. A chat reads as overheard; a pull-quote reads as supplied.
The before and after, measured. Two states of one thing, which is the claim a testimonial is actually making — frame-chart-bars would compare magnitudes instead.
The invitation. One action, not three.

local.label: Địa phương / thị trường
local.whenToUse: The story is WHERE. A new market, a service area, a route, one place against another. If the location is incidental, this is not the genre — pick the one that matches what you are actually claiming.

beats.beat: The place, first frame. A local video that opens on a logo spent its hook on the one thing the viewer already knows.
The question people THERE actually ask, then the answer. Skip it if you have no question worth turning a card for.
The number for this place next to the one people already carry — a national average, last year, the city next door. A local number with nothing beside it means nothing.
From where to where: expansion, delivery, a journey. Drop this beat if nothing moves — a route with one endpoint is a marker frame with extra steps.
Someone from there, named. Proof of place is a person, not a pin.
What to do and where. A service area or an address, not a slogan.

_notes: Two rules that hold across every genre, both learned from watching these render:
1. The hook is not a title card. A frame that names the topic without giving anything
away is a frame people scroll past. Lead with the verdict, the number or the result.
2. Do not use the same template twice in a row. validate-script.mjs already warns about
template variety, and the reason is that two identical frames read as a stall — the
viewer assumes the video has repeated itself and leaves.
